issues.description: The problem statement requires an instance method swiftExperienceDescription() that returns a String and instructs that the initializer should call this method and print its result. The template declares swiftExperienceDescription() with the signature -> String (extension in Developer.swift). However, the solution implements swiftExperienceDescription() returning Void and performs printing inside the method. This is a structural mismatch: the method return type differs between template/problem (String) and solution (Void), and the location of the printing (initializer vs method) differs. This inconsistency can confuse students (they will implement a method that returns String and expect to print its returned value, while the solution prints inside the method and returns Void) and may cause tests or example client code that expects a String result to behave incorrectly.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the solution align with the problem/template: change the solution's swiftExperienceDescription() to return a String (do not perform printing inside the method). Have the initializer call swiftExperienceDescription() and print the returned String (e.g. print(self.swiftExperienceDescription())). Alternatively, if the intended design is for the method to print directly and return Void, update the problem statement and the template signature to state that the method returns Void and prints the description. Prefer the first option to preserve the current exercise description and template.
